---
title: "sblr"
subtitle: "Scalable Bayesian Linear Regression"
---

`sblr` is an experimental R package for Bayesian genomic prediction and
variable selection. It supports individual-level PLINK BED genotypes, GWAS
summary statistics, sparse LD matrices, retained low-rank block-eigen LD operators, multi-trait
models, and annotation-informed priors.

::: {.callout-note title="Research software"}
The package is a research implementation and is not yet CRAN-ready. Its public
model names, operator contracts, fit schema, and seven canonical fitting
interfaces are stabilized and documented, but scientific analyses still need
appropriate chain lengths, sensitivity checks, and external validation.
:::

## Canonical fitting functions

```r
stblr_csr()
stblr_csr_annot()
stblr_block_eigen()
stblr_bed()

mtblr_csr()
mtblr_block_eigen()
mtblr_bed()
```

The STBLR functions fit scalar-trait models. The MTBLR functions fit one joint
multi-trait model per logical chain. Operators are prepared once per fit and
shared across deterministic logical chains.

The scalar block-eigen API defaults to retained low rank with
`eigen_prop = 0.995`; request `representation = "dense_reconstructed"` for the
historical packed reconstructed operator. The retained route is currently
single-trait only and preserves all priors and states in marker space.

Current log-variance BayesC-LV and BayesR-LV models are available for ST CSR
and retained block eigen only. BED-LV and MT-LV are not implemented. See
[Annotation-Informed Priors](methods/annotation_priors.qmd) for the current
capability table and clearly labelled proposed extensions.

## Model names

| Model | Prior kernel | Data level |
|---|---|---|
| `bayesc` | BayesC | individual level |
| `sbayesc` | BayesC | summary statistics |
| `bayesr` | BayesR | individual level |
| `sbayesr` | BayesR | summary statistics |
| `bayesrc` | annotation-informed BayesR | individual level |
| `sbayesrc` | annotation-informed BayesR | summary statistics |

The `s` prefix means **summary statistics**. It does not activate MAF-dependent
effect scaling.

`maf_effect_s` is a separate, optional MAF-dependent effect-variance control.
It can be used only on routes that explicitly support it; its value and MAF
provenance are recorded independently of the public model name. See the
[`maf_effect_s` guide](notes/maf_effect_s.qmd) for the scale definition and
support limits.

## Data representations and diagnostics

The canonical operators are packed BED for individual-level analysis, sparse
CSR LD for summary-statistics analysis, and block-eigen LD. Current scalar
block eigen uses retained factors by default, with reconstructed dense blocks
as an explicit historical/reference representation; current MT block eigen
uses reconstructed dense blocks. The [data-representation guide](notes/data_representations.qmd)
explains their scales, alignment requirements, and provenance.

Core convergence diagnostics cover the five trait-level variance traces.
Extended diagnostics cover applicable low-dimensional covariance,
probability, annotation, and sampled `maf_effect_s` parameters. Explicitly
selected markers can additionally retain effective-effect, binary-activity,
and mixture-component mixing diagnostics under a pre-execution memory guard.

Diagnostics assess MCMC mixing; they do not prove model correctness or
absolute convergence.
